pages: FICTIONAL TEST POLICY - NOT A REAL INSURANCE PRODUCT
Sample Health Shield (fictional) - policy wording for software testing only
1. PREAMBLE
This document is a fictional policy wording created to test the Policy-to-Patient prototype.
It does not describe any real insurer, product, price or benefit.
The policy covers inpatient hospitalisation expenses incurred in India during the policy year.
2. DEFINITIONS
Hospitalisation means admission to a hospital for a minimum of 24 consecutive hours.
Day care treatment means a procedure that needs less than 24 hours of admission due to technological advancement.
Policy year means a period of twelve months beginning on the policy start date.
Pre-existing disease means any condition diagnosed by a physician within 48 months before the policy start date.
Network hospital means a hospital that has an agreement with the insurer to provide cashless treatment.
3. SUM INSURED
The sum insured is Rs 5,00,000 per policy year on a floater basis for all insured members.
Claims paid during the policy year reduce the sum insured available for the rest of that year.
4. ROOM RENT
Room rent, boarding and nursing charges are covered up to Rs 5,000 per day.
Intensive care unit charges are covered up to Rs 10,000 per day.
If the insured person chooses a room above the eligible limit, the difference in room charges is payable by the insured person.
5. SUB-LIMITS
Cataract surgery is covered up to Rs 40,000 per eye.
Total knee replacement is covered up to Rs 2,00,000 per knee.
Treatment of kidney stones is covered up to Rs 50,000 per policy year.
6. PRE AND POST HOSPITALISATION
Medical expenses incurred up to 30 days before admission are covered.
Medical expenses incurred up to 60 days after discharge are covered.
These expenses are covered only if the main hospitalisation claim is admissible.
7. DAY CARE AND AMBULANCE
Day care treatments listed in the annexure are covered up to the sum insured.
Road ambulance charges are covered up to Rs 2,000 per hospitalisation.
8. DEDUCTIBLE
A deductible of Rs 10,000 applies to each policy year.
The insurer pays only the admissible amount above the deductible.
9. CO-PAYMENT
The insured person bears a co-payment of 10 percent of every admissible claim.
A co-payment of 20 percent applies if the insured person is aged 61 years or above at entry.
10. WAITING PERIODS
An initial waiting period of 30 days applies to all illnesses except accidents.
Pre-existing diseases are covered after a waiting period of 36 months of continuous coverage.
Hernia, cataract and joint replacement are covered after a waiting period of 24 months.
Maternity expenses are covered after a waiting period of 24 months.
11. MATERNITY
Maternity expenses are covered up to Rs 50,000 for a normal delivery or caesarean section.
Maternity cover is limited to two deliveries during the lifetime of the policy.
12. EXCLUSIONS
The insurer does not pay for cosmetic or plastic surgery unless needed after an accident.
Dental treatment is excluded unless it requires hospitalisation due to an accident.
Expenses for spectacles, contact lenses and hearing aids are excluded.
Treatment for injuries from participation in hazardous sports is excluded.
Experimental or unproven treatments are excluded.
13. CLAIMS PROCEDURE
For planned cashless treatment, the insured person must inform the insurer at least 48 hours before admission.
For emergency admission, the insurer must be informed within 24 hours of admission.
Reimbursement claims must be submitted within 30 days of discharge with original bills.
14. RENEWAL AND CANCELLATION
The policy is renewable for life if the premium is paid before the end of the grace period.
A grace period of 30 days is allowed for renewal.
The insured person may cancel a new policy within a free look period of 15 days.
15. GRIEVANCES
Complaints can be sent to the grievance cell of the insurer by email or letter.
The insurer will respond to a complaint within 14 days.
